title: Tensor counit compatibility with one K-flat representative
statement: Let $k:T\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with the recorded derived tensor structures [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure] and derived pullback [def-pc-derived-pullback]. Let $P$ and $G$ be cochain complexes of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], and suppose $P$ is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Let $\tau$ satisfy the canonical pullback tensor comparison predicate [def-pc-derived-pullback-tensor-comparison]. Write $H=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes G)$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and $\epsilon_k$ for the universal counit [def-pc-single-complex-base-change-stalk-condition]. There exist isomorphisms $a:Q(P)\otimes^LQ(G)\cong Q(H)$ and $b:Q(k^*H)\cong Lk^*Q(P)\otimes^LQ(k^*G)$ such that $Lk^*(a);\epsilon_k(H);b=\tau(Q(P),Q(G));(Lk^*Q(P)\otimes\epsilon_k(G))$. No K-flatness or boundedness is assumed on $G$.

proof.text: The canonical localization tensor map is invertible with the first factor P K-flat, giving a. Termwise tensor pullback commutes with the total tensor complex by its degreewise module comparison. Pullback preserves K-flatness, so the localization tensor map at k^*P and k^*G is invertible; the universal counit at P is invertible. Compose these isomorphisms to construct b.
For K-flat G the required equation is the defining coordinate equation of the canonical comparison, after canceling the invertible counit at P and the target localization tensor map.

For arbitrary G, take a K-flat resolution N -> G. Tensoring with P preserves this quasi-isomorphism. Naturality of the localization tensor maps, the termwise pullback tensor comparison, the universal counits and the canonical family τ gives the desired equation after precomposing by Lk^* of the induced derived tensor isomorphism. Cancel that isomorphism. Naturality uses the ordinary pulled-back map k^*N -> k^*G without requiring it to be a quasi-isomorphism.
